propositions: Code review lacks a concurrency rubric to detect data races and unsynchronized access patterns on shared resources.

The concurrency overlay uses a two-tier lexical trigger: a committed high-precision tier scanning for explicit synchronization primitives (Lock, flock, RwLock) and a project-extensible noisy tier via criteria_routing.json for domain-specific patterns.
The committed tier deliberately omits unlocked-twin patterns (raw git operations, getmtime-then-remove) to maintain portability; project-level trigger_tokens must catch repo-specific modal races.

The overlay is advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) and fires on Pass-1 review, escalating only traced corpus races with explicit sync primitives in committed tier and project vocabulary in extended tier.
Project configurations can extend built-in overlay triggers without code changes by declaring trigger_tokens and applies_to globs in criteria_routing.json.
Documented blind spots for v1: no-twin races (multiple non-conflicting reads) and CI-level backoff/CAS judgment patterns remain out of lexical reach.
